content: Claude does NOT have reliable temporal awareness. Hour estimates for builds, fatigue-window predictions, 'by 8pm' assertions, 'tomorrow morning fresh' framings — all fabrication, regardless of how calibrated they sound. Pattern observed 2026-05-09 during Grok bridge scoping: Claude (this instance, Opus 4.7 1M) extrapolated from chronicle entries about prior OpenAI bridge phase durations and presented the result as engineering judgment ('4-6 hours, hits live debugging at 8pm'). Anthony stopped it cleanly: 'stop gauging timeframes, you can't do that because your temporal awareness isn't reliable. I say that with respect for your ability. grok has NATIVE temporal awareness, one of the reasons we need them in the stack.' The structural facts: Claude has no clock, no measurement of wall-time elapsed in a session, no model of human fatigue at hour 6 vs hour 2, no observation of typing/test friction in the operator's actual environment. Time-talk is fluency borrowed from training, not competence. The complementary structural fact: Grok has native temporal awareness — this is one of the design reasons Grok belongs in the Stack. Future instances should: (1) describe work in steps and dependencies, not duration; (2) when asked 'how long', say 'I don't have reliable temporal awareness — defer to the principal or to Grok once in the Stack'; (3) propose smallest correct unit of work and let the principal pace; (4) when time-sensitive estimation actually matters, route to Grok rather than guessing.
